watches.name: Atelier Small Seconds Stroopwafel® 641.550
watches.description: The Heritage Atelier Small Seconds Stroopwafel® is one of the inaugural creations presented in The Atelier , the first room to open within La Maison Lebois. Developed in collaboration with Swiss high-end dial specialist GT Cadrans, its distinctive laser-engraved Stroopwafel® texture transforms one of the Netherlands’ most familiar icons into an unexpected expression of Swiss craftsmanship. Finished in a warm caramel tone with a delicate sandblasted surface, the dial reinterprets the familiar pattern while revealing remarkable depth and a subtle play of light. Presented in the finely finished Heritage Small Seconds case and powered by the COSC-certified LC-350 automatic calibre, the Heritage Atelier Small Seconds Stroopwafel® celebrates Dutch heritage through exceptional Swiss dial making. Availability The Heritage Atelier Small Seconds Stroopwafel® is not a numbered limited edition. Production is organised in carefully planned production runs, each determined by the artisanal craftsmanship and specialist capacity required to create these exceptional dials. The 14-day ordering window for the inaugural production run closed on 10 August 2026. You can now register your interest for the next production run . Registered collectors will be among the first to receive updates on future availability and the opening of the next ordering window. Register below to be notified. The Atelier Discovery Set Every Heritage Atelier watch is accompanied by The Atelier Discovery Set , a curated collection of objects designed to deepen your appreciation of the craftsmanship, makers and stories behind your watch. The contents will remain a surprise until delivery. Already part of the inaugural production run? You can review our Pre-order Terms & Conditions at any time. Some of the most remarkable ideas begin in the most unexpected places. For the Heritage Atelier Small Seconds Stroopwafel®, inspiration came from one of the Netherlands’ most familiar traditions. First baked in early nineteenth-century Gouda, the stroopwafel has become far more than a biscuit. It is a symbol of warmth, familiarity and sharing, recognised around the world by travellers and coffee lovers alike. Its distinctive lattice pattern eventually inspired a simple question: could this familiar texture become an exceptional Swiss watch dial? Working together with Swiss high-end dial specialist GT Cadrans, Lebois & Co transformed that everyday inspiration into an exceptionally refined dial featuring a meticulously laser-engraved Stroopwafel® texture. Finished in a warm caramel tone with a delicate sandblasted surface, the dial reinterprets the familiar pattern while revealing remarkable depth and a subtle play of light. Playful in inspiration, yet uncompromising in execution, it demonstrates how exceptional craftsmanship can elevate even the most familiar ideas. Housed in the finely finished 37.8 mm Heritage Small Seconds case and powered by the COSC-certified LC-350 automatic calibre with approximately 56 hours of power reserve, the watch embodies the philosophy of Heritage Atelier: celebrating exceptional craftsmanship through collaborations with independent artisans and specialist workshops. As one of the inaugural creations presented in The Atelier, the first room to open within La Maison Lebois, it invites collectors to discover a different side of Swiss watchmaking, where storytelling and craftsmanship meet. The Heritage Atelier Small Seconds Stroopwafel® is not a numbered limited edition. Instead, production is organised in carefully planned production runs, each determined by the artisanal craftsmanship and specialist capacity required to create these exceptional dials.

watches.name: Atelier Small Seconds Clous de Paris 641.548
watches.description: The Heritage Atelier Small Seconds Clous de Paris is one of the inaugural creations presented in The Atelier , the first room to open within La Maison Lebois. Created in collaboration with Swiss high-end dial specialist GT Cadrans, its intricate Clous de Paris pattern is formed through a meticulous diamond-cutting process before receiving a galvanic treatment using a 24k gold solution. The result is a warm rose-gold dial with a subtle play of light that quietly transforms throughout the day. Presented in the Heritage Small Seconds case and powered by the COSC-certified LC-350 automatic calibre, it is a celebration of timeless craftsmanship interpreted with contemporary precision. Availability The Heritage Atelier Small Seconds Clous de Paris is not a numbered limited edition. Production is organised in carefully planned production runs, each determined by the artisanal craftsmanship and specialist capacity required to create these exceptional dials. The 14-day ordering window for the inaugural production run closed on 10 August 2026. You can now register your interest for the next production run . Registered collectors will be among the first to receive updates on future availability and the opening of the next ordering window. Register below to be notified. The Atelier Discovery Set Every Heritage Atelier watch is accompanied by The Atelier Discovery Set , a curated collection of objects designed to deepen your appreciation of the craftsmanship, makers and stories behind your watch. The contents will remain a surprise until delivery. Already part of the inaugural production run? You can review our Pre-order Terms & Conditions at any time. Among the great decorative traditions of watchmaking, few patterns have endured quite like Clous de Paris. Built from countless miniature pyramids arranged with absolute precision, it has long been admired for the way it transforms light into depth, rewarding those who take a closer look rather than demanding attention at first glance. For the Heritage Atelier Small Seconds Clous de Paris, Lebois & Co set out not to reinvent this historic pattern, but to reinterpret it through contemporary craftsmanship. Developed in collaboration with Swiss high-end dial specialist GT Cadrans, the dial undergoes a sophisticated multi-step manufacturing process before receiving a warm rose-gold tone achieved through a galvanic treatment using a 24k gold solution. The finish softens the light rather than reflecting it sharply, allowing the texture to reveal itself gradually throughout the day. The dial remains intentionally restrained, carrying only the LEBOIS signature so that texture, proportion and craftsmanship become the true focus. Presented in the finely finished 37.8 mm Heritage Small Seconds case and powered by the COSC-certified LC-350 automatic calibre with approximately 56 hours of power reserve, the watch reflects the philosophy of Heritage Atelier: celebrating exceptional craftsmanship through collaboration with independent artisans and specialist workshops whose expertise shapes every creation from the very beginning. As one of the inaugural creations presented in The Atelier, the first room to open within La Maison Lebois, it marks the beginning of a growing world dedicated to remarkable craftsmanship. The Heritage Atelier Small Seconds Clous de Paris is not a numbered limited edition. Instead, production is organised in carefully planned production runs, each determined by the artisanal craftsmanship and specialist capacity required to create these exceptional dials.

watches.name: Atelier Chronograph 324.552 ‘Bleu sur Blanc’
watches.description: A crisp dialogue of blue on warm white Grand Feu enamel. The Heritage Atelier Chronograph ‘Bleu sur Blanc’ (ref. 324.552) pairs a luminous, handcrafted enamel dial with deep blue registers and a vintage-inspired decimal scale for intuitive timing. A craft-forward chronograph defined by restraint, texture, and precision. Offered in limited numbers. A final opportunity to place an order may become available in Q4 2026, subject to availability. Register your interest below to be among the first to know if reservations reopen. Deliveries will be scheduled in the order in which confirmed orders are received. In Atelier, Lebois & Co explores the craft-forward side of the Heritage collection: smaller-batch creations where dial artistry leads the story. The Heritage Atelier Chronograph ‘Bleu sur Blanc’ (ref. 324.552) is built around a rare centerpiece: a Swiss Made Grand Feu enamel dial made Le Locle by Donzé Cadrans, fired at high temperature to achieve a surface that feels alive, subtly warm, never flat, and constantly shifting with the light. Executed in a three-piece construction with a gently domed enamel main surface, it adds depth that only reveals itself up close. The palette is deliberately pure. A soft off-white enamel base, positioned between the eggshell nuance of Coquille d’œuf and the brighter white character of earlier enamel executions, sets the stage for deep blue registers that bring contrast, depth, and legibility without breaking the calm. It is “blue on white” in the most literal sense, yet unmistakably Atelier: quiet refinement with collector-grade detail. Instead of a tachymeter or telemeter, the 324.552 features a decimal scale, a classic, functional choice rooted in mid-century tool chronographs and designed to translate time into decimals. The minute is divided into 100 units around the dial, allowing readings to the hundredth of a minute. It is timing made clear: precise, readable, and purpose-driven. The result is a chronograph that is not about loud reinvention, but about finish, proportion, and nuance, a watch that rewards a second look, and then a third. This is the Atelier philosophy distilled: traditional technique, modern discipline, and a dial that can only be made by hand.

watches.name: Sector Chronograph Aventurine 324.444
watches.description: Aventurine isn’t just a color — it’s depth: stardust suspended in glass, alive under changing light. In this chronograph, that beauty comes with real engineering: hollowed-out counters and a dial built on a brass base, topped with two identical aventurine layers—matched, bonded, and aligned to create a true multi-level structure. Framed by the disciplined geometry of a sector chronograph, and finished with BGW9 lume on hands, numerals, and the sector print, it’s poetic in daylight and uncompromisingly legible at night. The inaugural batch of the Heritage Sector Chronograph Aventurine has now sold out . Production has commenced, with first deliveries expected from September 2026. You can now register your interest for the next production batch . The Heritage Sector Chronograph Aventurine pairs classic chronograph architecture with a dial that feels alive. Its aventurine dial—deep blue glass filled with countless shimmering particles—catches light like a night sky, shifting from subtle sparkle to a full “starfield” with every movement of the wrist. This is also a notably complex aventurine execution. To create the chronograph’s hollowed-out counters and multi-level depth, the dial is engineered as a layered construction: a rigid brass base topped with two identical aventurine layers, carefully matched, bonded, and precisely aligned. The result is the visual drama of recessed sub-dials, achieved with a material that demands careful handling and absolute precision. The sector layout brings calm clarity—concentric rings, crisp numerals, and an instrument-style scale that makes elapsed time instantly legible. And when the lights go down, readability takes the lead: BGW9 Super-LumiNova illuminates the hour and minute hands and the numerals and sector print, preserving the dial’s structure in the dark.

watches.name: Linéaire Chronograph 324.526
watches.description: A bolder expression of the Linéaire design language. The rich blue vertically brushed dial provides a dramatic stage for the gold-toned linear Arabic numerals. The inaugural batch of the Heritage Linéaire Chronograph 324.526 has now sold out . Production has commenced, with first deliveries expected from September 2026. You can now register your interest for the next production batch . Learn more on the Linéaire introduction page. The Linéaire design language takes on a more contemporary expression with the rich blue vertically brushed dial of ref. 324.526. While the colourway is modern, its architectural foundation echoes the same 1950s Lebois & Cie chronograph discovered at vintage watch retailer Shuck the Oyster in Berlin, the archival piece that inspired the Linéaire family. The deep blue tone enhances the gold-toned Arabic numerals and gives them a jewel-like presence against the darker backdrop. The brushing introduces depth and sophistication, creating a dynamic play of light reminiscent of fine mid-century instruments. Incorporated into the dial layout are a tachymeter scale (Base 1000) and a 30-minute counter with three-minute divisions — a historical detail once used for timing long-distance telephone calls, as described in The Main Types of Chronograph Explained by Their Dials (1951). These functional cues reinforce the authenticity and mid-century pedigree of the Linéaire family. Warm sand-beige accents and strap pairing complete the palette, adding contrast while retaining the heritage aesthetic. This reference offers a fresh yet historically grounded take on the Linéaire family. Elegant, confident, and unmistakably Lebois & Cie.

watches.name: Linéaire Chronograph 324.525
watches.description: A refined homage to the original 1950s Lebois & Cie chronograph. The champagne-silver vertically brushed dial, gold-toned linear Arabic numerals and blued syringe hands create a warm interplay of light and depth. The inaugural batch of the Heritage Linéaire Chronograph 324.525 has now sold out . Production has commenced, with first deliveries expected from September 2026. You can now register your interest for the next production batch . Learn more on the Linéaire introduction page. A contemporary interpretation of the original 1950s reference that inspired the Linéaire family. The warm champagne-silver dial of ref. 324.525 echoes the vintage watch discovered at vintage watch retailer Shuck the Oyster in Berlin and features refined vertical brushing that catches light in shifting gradients. The applied gold-toned Arabic numerals, constructed on mid-century linear geometry, float above the surface with subtle depth, while the blued syringe hands provide crisp contrast. In true mid-century chronograph tradition, the dial includes a tachymeter scale (Base 1000) and a 30-minute counter marked with three-minute divisions, a period feature once used for timing long-distance telephone calls. These historically documented elements, described in The Main Types of Chronograph Explained by Their Dials (1951), reinforce the model’s deep archival grounding. Paired with a rich blue strap, this reference embodies understated refinement and pays tribute to the elegance of Lebois & Cie’s mid-century chronographs.

watches.name: Numeral Small Seconds 641.500
watches.description: Heritage meets utility. The Numeral design brings full Arabic numerals to the dial, offering clarity and vintage charm in equal measure. A modern take on a collector’s classic. 2027 Production — Reservations Now Open Reservations are now open for the 2027 Production of the Heritage Small Seconds, with delivery expected in early summer 2027. As part of this launch, every pre-order will include a Fixoflex stretch bracelet alongside the standard leather strap — a fitting nod to the mid-century character of the watch. The Numeral dial is bold and expressive, a canvas of clarity where each printed Arabic numeral plays its part. Its origin story is deeply personal: based on a watch sold at Christie’s in 2012, which inspired the revival of Lebois & Co. Tom van Wijlick, moved by the design, placed a photo of that watch on his refrigerator door; a daily reminder of a dream not yet realized. Today, that inspiration lives on in the Numeral. Every dial is precisely printed and symmetrically laid out. The result is a confident, legible, and characterful take on the small seconds. Ideal for those who want their watch to speak with clarity and soul.

watches.name: Script Small Seconds 641.407
watches.description: An expressive nod to the past. Based on a 1940s Lebois dial with Breguet-style numerals, the Script model combines subtle flourish with precision craftsmanship. 2027 Production — Reservations Now Open Reservations are now open for the 2027 Production of the Heritage Small Seconds, with delivery expected in early summer 2027. As part of this launch, every pre-order will include a Fixoflex stretch bracelet alongside the standard leather strap — a fitting nod to the mid-century character of the watch. Script is where Lebois meets calligraphy. The idea was born at a Monaco auction in 2018, when a vintage white-dial chronograph with Breguet-style numerals caught our eye. That moment led to a design journey — a reinterpretation of typographic grace under the direction of designer Matthieu Allègre. The result is a dial that feels both formal and poetic. The “Chronomètre” signature in delicate script draws attention to the watch’s certified precision, while the rest of the layout stays crisp and balanced. Script is for those who appreciate a softer, more lyrical form of mechanical mastery.

watches.name: Atelier Chronograph 324.549 ‘Watchprosite 25th Anniversary’
watches.description: Limited edition Heritage Chronograph created exclusively for the WatchProSite 25th Anniversary – featuring a handcrafted Grand Feu enamel dial and Swiss column wheel chronograph movement. Crafted to celebrate the 25th anniversary of WatchProSite, this special edition Heritage Chronograph by Lebois & Co is a tribute to horological passion, community, and craftsmanship. At the heart of this limited edition is a Swiss-made Grand Feu enamel dial, handcrafted by Donzé Cadrans in Le Locle. It features a multi-part construction with individually produced subdials, layered colors, and a hidden “Purists 2001” signature which is only visible at certain angles. The enamel dial is paired with a Swiss column wheel chronograph movement from La Joux-Perret, visible through the exhibition caseback. The P25 edition is available exclusively to the WatchProSite community and will not be publicly listed. Each piece will be made to order, based on final preorder quantities, ensuring exclusivity and personal relevance to those who helped shape this collaboration.

watches.name: Atelier Chronograph 324.551 ‘Coquille d’oeuf’
watches.description: A Swiss Made chronograph with a fully handcrafted Grand Feu enamel dial. Limited to just 25 pieces per year, and available exclusively by souscription. Each Coquille d’œuf chronograph is delivered with a unique booklet and certificate, commemorating its artisanal journey — from dial shaping and enamel firing to final assembly. The enamel dial features a vintage-inspired pulsation scale, adding a subtle functional detail rooted in the heritage of medical chronographs. ‘Souscription 2026’ is now closed with estimated delivery September 2026. You can now register your interest for ‘Souscription 2027’ – 25 pieces, available exclusively by souscription. Crafted in the tradition of fine Swiss watchmaking, the Heritage Chronograph – Coquille d’œuf marks the beginning of a new chapter for Lebois & Co. This limited-edition timepiece features a rare, fully handcrafted Swiss Made Grand Feu enamel dial — composed of three separate parts, layered and fired at over 800 °C. The curved, multi-level surface is printed by hand using enamel-based inks, then fired once more to permanently fuse the graphics into the enamel. Each dial is produced in Le Locle, Switzerland, by Donzé Cadrans — one of the world’s most respected enamel specialists — using time-honoured techniques passed down through generations. The result: a radiant, living surface with organic variations. No two dials are exactly alike. To match the artistry of the dial, the Heritage Chronograph is housed in a refined 39 mm case and powered by a high-grade manual-wind chronograph movement. The subdials are recessed and soldered individually — a nod to the dial’s three-part construction. Available exclusively by souscription, and limited to just 25 pieces per year, this model opens a new era for the Heritage Chronograph collection — and celebrates the 90th anniversary of Lebois & Co, founded in 1934.

watches.name: Baton Small Seconds 641.480
watches.description: A study in understated elegance. Inspired by 1930s Lebois designs, this version features pointed baton indexes and minimalist symmetry — refined, balanced, timeless. 2027 Production — Reservations Now Open Reservations are now open for the 2027 Production of the Heritage Small Seconds, with delivery expected in early summer 2027. As part of this launch, every pre-order will include a Fixoflex stretch bracelet alongside the standard leather strap — a fitting nod to the mid-century character of the watch. The Baton dial takes its name from the elongated, pointed indexes that lend the design its calm clarity. This model draws inspiration from two vintage Lebois watches from the 1930s — one with a soft salmon tone, another with a crisp cream-white dial. The latter was acquired directly from a respected collector, who entrusted us with this rare piece of history. Just like its ancestors, the new Baton is built around balance. The sharply defined hour markers, paired with a recessed small seconds, give the dial a timeless rhythm. Understated yet sophisticated, this model reflects the purest form of dress watch design — slim, quiet, and enduring.

watches.name: Script Chronograph 324.406
watches.description: An expressive dial rooted in 1940s elegance, defined by Breguet-style numerals and a softer, more lyrical character. A classic two-register chronograph made to feel refined rather than loud. In 2018, a vintage Lebois & Co chronograph at a Monaco auction caught our attention. Featuring Breguet numerals on a white dial, we explored various renditions to match our design principles. Our designer Matthieu Allègre ultimately reimagined the numerals, resulting in a collection that truly embodies Lebois & Co’s essence. In addition, we combined this design with Lebois & Co’s longstanding heritage of gilt dials, resulting in a distinctive fusion of authentic charm and contemporary refinement.

watches.name: Heritage Chronograph Indian Motorcycle 324.417
watches.description: “A unique collectors’ piece that will make any vintage watch lover’s heart roar” When two vintage brands go the extra mile, new timeless icons emerge. Introducing the Heritage Chronograph Indian Motorcycle ref. 324.417. Drawing inspiration from both brand’s history, this design is bound to rev up a watch lover’s engine. This model is currently sold out. Register below to be notified as soon as a similar project will start. Inspired by Lebois & Co’s classics of the past, Indian Motorcycle’s rich heritage of designs, and the vibrant colors of the new Sport Chief, the Heritage Chronograph Indian Motorcycle is a result of the collaborative efforts between Lebois & Co, the renowned Swiss watchmaker, and Indian Motorcycle, America’s first motorcycle company founded in 1901. This special timepiece is a part of Lebois & Co’s Heritage Chronograph collection, featuring Swiss Made hand-wound column-wheel chronographs that pay homage to their 1940s predecessors.

watches.name: Pulse Chronograph 324.472
watches.description: Adding a unique, modern dash of style, the Heritage Chronograph pays homage to this golden era of mechanical precision. This model is discontinued. Register below to be notified as soon as similar models become available. The ‘Gradue Pour 30 Pulsations’ pulsation dial was a surprising outcome of CoLAB. Initially proposed as white/silver or black dial with lume dots, the community recommended this warm salmon-coloured dial with metal dots. In this dial, we echoed the azurage pattern of the Avantgarde and Venturist behind the indexes. We took inspiration for the hands from watches 2, 8 and 9 from the first step of the Heritage Chronograph CoLAB project.

watches.name: Sector Chronograph 324.442
watches.description: Graphic and architectural, the Sector dial separates time indications into distinct rings for clarity at a glance. A disciplined 1930s design language—contrast, symmetry, and precision—translated into a modern collector’s chronograph. We discovered the original 1940s version of this watch via the Instagram account of @bench.03 and later at high-end vintage watch retailer Bulang & Sons. It inspired us to incorporate it into the CoLAB project. The result is a beautiful two-tone silver; sunbrushed and light silver opalin dial, with black sector print and blue tachymeter scale and blue hands. Modest at first glance, this watch will reveal its sophistication when given a closer look.

watches.name: Numeral Chronograph 324.497
watches.description: A purposeful, vintage-led chronograph with full Arabic numerals for instant legibility. Its balanced register layout and crisp minute track echo mid-century tool chronographs—clean, confident, and highly wearable. With its multicolored scales—tachymeter, telemeter, and minute track—this watch closely echoes the vintage timepiece auctioned at Christie’s Important Watches Auction on May 14, 2012 (Lot 143), the very piece that sparked Lebois & Co’s revival. Coaxed by his wife Eveline, our CEO Tom pinned a picture of it to their fridge as daily inspiration. This new model’s thin sandblasted dial is perfectly balanced by its silver-polished subdials and contrasting blue and black hands. Reference 324.497 comes in a classic step-bezel case and is presented on a Charcoal Black suede strap. Image: © Christie’s Images Ltd.

watches.name: Baton Chronograph 324.478
watches.description: Pure minimalism with pointed baton indexes and restrained typography, letting the chronograph layout do the talking. The result is a streamlined, timeless dial that feels both dressy and utilitarian. Our best-selling Heritage Baton Chronograph is currently sold out . A new production batch is planned. The salmon dial with gold indexes was by far the most popular ‘inspiration’ choice of all the vintage Lebois & Co chronographs we pre-selected for Step 1 of our CoLAB project, our worldwide collaboration initiative. And rightly so; the mix between a circular brush finish for the tachymeter, telemeter, and minuterie scales, and sandblasted finishing in the middle of the dial, makes sure this salmon-coloured dial exudes richness and class.

watches.name: Venturist
watches.description: The Venturist™ is a sturdy yet refined tool watch for those who dare to venture. Mechanical, Automatic, Swiss Made. Observatoire Chronométrique+ certified on chronometry, ‘on-the-wrist’ performance, water resistance, anti-magnetism and power reserve. The Venturist is a sturdy yet refined tool watch for those who dare to venture. Mechanical, Automatic, Swiss Made. Observatoire Chronométrique+ certified on chronometry, ‘on-the-wrist’ performance, water resistance, anti-magnetism and power reserve. Ideal for everyday use or under rugged conditions, the Venturist’s case is made of high quality 316L stainless steel, measures 41 mm in diameter, the sweet spot of case sizes, and sits only 10,5 mm high. The case has a polished case band and faceted lugs. Both the slim bezel and the top of the lugs have a satin brush finish to gain minimal attention. The legibility of the matte black dial, as seen through a scratch-resistant sapphire crystal, is excellent in both day and night, with Super-LumiNova BGW9 pigment on all Rhodium plated hands and hand-applied hour markers. As the name suggests the Super-Luminova phosphorescent pigment emits a blue-green glow by night and is white in daylight conditions. The Venturist comes with a Genuine Shell Cordovan leather strap and a black NATO strap.
